More than half of the final stories must originate with independent, local or social discovery, using the first source in each story as the discovery source; established outlets may account for no more than half.

items.title: Supreme Court Collegium recommends appointment of 7 advocates as Madhya Pradesh High Court judges
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium has recommended the appointment of seven advocates as judges of the Madhya Pradesh High Court. The decision was taken at a meeting of the Collegium held on October 26, 2026. The advocates recommended for elevation are: Vivek Sharan Rajesh Kumar Shukla Kanak Gaharwar alias Kanak Lata Singh Bhakti Vyas Shreyas Pandit Mrinal Elker alias Mrinal Mazumdar Avinash Zargar The Collegium's recommendations will now be forwarded to the Central government for further processing. The appointments will take effect once the Central government clears the recommendations and the President of India issues the necessary warrants of appointment. The Madhya Pradesh High Court has a sanctioned strength of 53 judges. According to data for September 2026, the High Court was functioning with 38 judges, leaving 15 posts vacant, representing a vacancy rate of approximately 28 per cent. [Read Collegium Resolution]

items.title: Supreme Court Collegium recommends elevation of CESTAT judicial member as Bombay High Court judge
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium has recommended two names for appointment as judges of the Bombay High Court, including a judicial member of the Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT) in Mumbai. The Collegium cleared the proposal during its meeting held today, October 26, 2026. The two persons recommended for elevation are: Ajay Sharma , judicial member at the Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT) in Mumbai. Vaibhav Anant Sugdare , a practising advocate. If these recommendations are cleared by the Central government, the working strength of the Bombay High Court will increase to 77 judges. [Read Collegium Resolution]

items.title: Supreme Court Collegium recommends 4 High Court judges for elevation as Chief Justices
items.summary: The Supreme Court Collegium on Monday recommended the elevation of four High Court judges as Chief Justices of various High Courts. According to a resolution issued on October 26, Justice Manash Ranjan Pathak of the Gujarat High Court has been recommended for appointment as Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court. Justice P Sam Koshy of the Telangana High Court has been recommended as Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court, while Calcutta High Court judge Justice Tapabrata Chakraborty has been recommended for appointment as Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court. The Collegium has also recommended Patna High Court judge Justice Sudhir Singh for appointment as Chief Justice of the Uttarakhand High Court. [Read Collegium Resolution]
